# Physics (class 10 / 12), ~2 minutes, written by Claude for F-014 S4 (hard topics). Expect: a content slide on light;
# "refractory bricks" and "refraction of sound" are traps; "let me show you the refraction of light" opens simulation
# mode; air into glass at 30 degrees, glass 1.5: theta2 19.5 degrees, critical angle not printed (n1 < n2); then glass
# into air at 50 degrees: total internal reflection, critical angle 41.8 degrees; a prism is a notice; back to the slides.
@setup subject="Physics" grade=10 topic="Refraction of light"

Good morning. Today we study what happens when light passes from one medium into another.
[pause 1]
Furnaces are lined with refractory bricks, and sound also bends in air, but today we only talk about light.
[pause 1.5]
Let me show you the refraction of light.
A ray of light goes from air into glass at an angle of incidence of 30 degrees.
The refractive index of glass is 1.5.
[pause 1]
The ray bends towards the normal because glass is optically denser than air.
Snell's law says n1 sin theta1 equals n2 sin theta2.
[pause 1.5]
Now the light goes from glass into air.
Let us increase the angle of incidence to 50 degrees.
Beyond the critical angle there is no refracted ray at all, and all the light is reflected back.
This is total internal reflection, and optical fibres use it.
[pause 1]
In a prism different colours bend by different amounts, but that is dispersion, for the next class.
[pause 1.5]
Okay, let's get back to the slides.
[pause 1]
So light bends towards the normal entering a denser medium and away from it leaving one.
